newsitem.title: USA: G30 proposes systemic safeguards, global supervisor.
newsitem.headline: G30 proposes systemic safeguards, global supervisor.

text.p: The Group of Thirty on Friday unveiled its proposals for managing global financial risk, including an umbrella supervisor, standardized reporting and accounting standards and tighter laws governing international transactions.

Leaders of the international financial group at a press conference at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York cited the rapid pace of financial globalization and the relatively slow pace of official reaction.
"There is an inherent contradiction in national supervision of global markets and global firms," said John Heimann, chariman of global financial institutions at Merrill Lynch.
"The marketplace is coming together ... and yet you have geographic and functional separation among regulators," he added.
The G30 report, resulting from 18 months of work, aims to avert serious disruptions to the global financial system.

But the proposals for standardized reporting would also cut costs for international institutions, which they could pass on to consumers, said New York Fed President William McDonough, a signatory of the report.
"We very much welcome this report," McDonough said. "We are very sympathetic with its conclusions."
--an industry standing committee to spearhead development of global risk management principles and improved disclosure
--a lead coordinator for all global financial institutions
--standards for exchanges, clearinghouses and settlement systems, including risk management and financial stability; protection of customer assets; enforceability of netting and contracts
